projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 19–24 device count paired with zero indoor camera motion strongly suggests the household is gathered outdoors rather than inside, or indicates a network/presence tracking anomaly. Given the unusually high device count for a family of four, a quick verification is recommended to rule out a false signal or unlogged guests.

The sustained 22–24 device count paired with zero camera motion strongly suggests a large, stationary gathering rather than typical movement, but the unusually high count warrants verifying that all connections are legitimate guests to rule out unauthorized network access.

The sustained 22–27 device count over four hours on a Sunday afternoon, paired with zero camera triggers, strongly indicates a large gathering is occurring in camera-blind zones rather than a network glitch. This matters because it confirms an active event in unmonitored areas, prompting Steve to verify guest locations and ensure perimeter/security cameras are operational.

The mobile device count has climbed to 27 while cameras remain completely inactive, strongly indicating either an unannounced gathering of guests or a camera system outage/misconfiguration. Steve should verify camera functionality and confirm if visitors are expected to ensure security and system health.

The sustained presence of 19–23 mobile devices over four hours directly contradicts the complete lack of camera activity, strongly indicating a camera system outage, disabled feeds, or a network segmentation issue rather than an occupied home.

The consistently high mobile device count (20–23) over a three-hour Sunday morning window, combined with zero camera motion, strongly indicates a large group of guests or extended family gathered indoors. This explains the network load and confirms normal weekend hosting rather than a device or security anomaly.

The stable device count (25–27) combined with zero camera motion and confirmed sleep metrics confirms the entire household is in a deep sleep state; the high device count is consistent with children’s electronics and smart home infrastructure rather than nighttime activity.

The sustained high device count (23–27) combined with zero camera motion late Saturday night indicates stationary occupancy, likely with family or guests settled in non-camera zones like bedrooms; the gradual device increase confirms late-night connectivity typical of a weekend gathering, which is normal.

The drop in connected devices to a stable 23 at 19:04, paired with prolonged camera stillness, indicates the household has settled into a low-activity evening routine rather than departing or experiencing an intrusion, confirming the earlier correlation is benign.

The sustained 23–25 device count paired with zero camera motion over the last 90 minutes indicates a settled Saturday evening gathering (likely a movie night, gaming session, or extended family/friends visiting) where occupants are stationary in non-camera zones. This aligns with normal weekend patterns and requires no action.
